threads.body: [Testing] Test code should not add `@Nullable` annotations. Please remove both parameter annotations here and the now-unused import.

replies.body:
Addressed in de40c45b2376b09cec15427f63ec82e2a10b7576.

Analysis: The nullable values remain valid Java arguments without test-code annotations. Removing the two parameter annotations also leaves the import unused, so the import must be removed with them.

Upsides: The shared test fixture follows the repository rule against `@Nullable` in test code and no longer carries an unused import.

Downsides: The method signature no longer documents nullability through annotations, but its callers and conditional expected values make that use clear.

threads.body: The new formatter's credential/path/query stripping and IPv6 bracket handling are not exercised by the localhost integration tests. Please add focused unit coverage for null/empty endpoints, absent ports, IPv6, and credential/path/query removal, analogous to `ElasticsearchServerTargetTest`, so malformed targets or sensitive host text cannot regress unnoticed.

replies.body:
Addressed in e10203dd7d1972a6352e59ddecddff3f35638f32.

Analysis: The integration tests use normal localhost endpoints and cannot exercise the formatter's sanitization branches. A plain Java unit-test module can load the javaagent helper directly without the instrumented test class loader hiding its nested Endpoint class.

Upsides: The tests now cover null and empty endpoint lists, absent ports, single and grouped IPv6 addresses, credential stripping, path/query/fragment stripping, and malformed sanitized hosts. Sensitive input and invalid targets can no longer regress without a focused test failure.

Downsides: The new unit-test module adds a small amount of Gradle configuration and test execution time.
